newsitem.title: GERMANY: Mercedes cuts costs at German factory.
newsitem.headline: Mercedes cuts costs at German factory.

text.p: German vehicle maker Mercedes-Benz AG said Monday it reached a pact on cost-cutting measures at its Kassel factory aimed at saving tens of millions of marks in costs.

A spokesman at Mercedes, a unit of German industrial group Daimler-Benz AG, said the 2,800 workers at the plant agreed to five percent wage cuts for four years beginning in January 1996 and also more flexible working hours.
In exchange, Mercedes said it would not lay off any workers at the facility through to the end of 2000.
The Mercedes spokesman said the cost savings could total up to 24 million marks each year.

The Kassel factory produces axles for commercial vehicles produced by Mercedes. The cost-cutting measures come as part of Mercedes' aim to cut one billion marks each year in expenses in the commercial vehicle division.
Half of the cost savings are expected to come from the introduction of the new Actros lorry, which is being unveiled this week at the IAA truck exhibition in Hanover.
Talks were still underway at the other Mercedes commercial vehicle factories in Germany in the cities of Woerth and Mannheim, the company spokesman said.
